items.title: DeepSeek's Open-Source Harness Framework, Deconstructed: Beyond V4 Pro, the Bigger Shift Lies in the Plugin Architecture
items.summary_1line: DeepSeek's Open-Source Harness Framework, Deconstructed: Beyond V4 Pro, the Bigger Shift Lies in the Plugin Architecture finance.biggo.com
items.editor_note: Latest deep dive: argues the plugin architecture, not the underlying V4 Pro model, is the bigger shift.

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek open-sourced Harness in mid-August as an MIT-licensed agent framework where models, tools, and skills are all plugins, drawing immediate comparisons to Claude Cowork. A fast release cadence followed — a v0.1 preview, then a 14-change post-beta update adding multimodal and subagent support — before Harness began orchestrating rival coding agents instead of just running its own.
editorial.whats_new: An Aug. 24 deep dive argues DeepSeek Harness's plugin architecture, not the underlying V4 Pro model, is the real shift — days after Harness added Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents to pitch itself as an agent-era scheduling layer.
editorial.why_it_matters: Harness is shaping up as MIT-licensed, open agent-runtime infrastructure that can host Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents — a real alternative orchestration layer to evaluate, not just another model wrapper.
editorial.take_for_builders: Prototype against Harness's plugin/subagent interface before standardizing on a closed agent runtime — its MIT license and ability to host Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents make it a viable orchestration-layer alternative worth a bake-off.

status.detail: Harness moved from open-source launch to orchestrating rival coding agents as sub-agents within eight days.
